approvedDecisions.resolution: Keep full decimal precision until each charge or credit posts. Round each posted amount to the nearest currency minor unit, with ties away from zero. Sum posted amounts at full precision.
If the configured due day does not exist in a month, use the last calendar day in Asia/Dubai. Preserve the configured due day for later months.
Count the Dubai notice submission date as day one. With a 30-day notice received on June 1, June 30 is the earliest move-out date without a notice deduction.
For each room transfer, the manager records the rent difference, deposit treatment, and cancellation terms. Both parties confirm the terms before the transfer takes effect.

If no destination is agreed within seven calendar days, the manager can extend the room-change deadline once by seven calendar days. Close the request if no agreement exists at the applicable deadline and the manager grants no extension. The tenant stays in their current room when the request closes without an agreement.

For late-payment extensions and room changes, the next approval is allowed from the same Dubai calendar day six months after the manager’s approval. If the target month lacks that day, use its last day. The two limits are independent.
Once approved by a manager, a late-payment extension or room change counts toward its own six-month limit even if the tenant withdraws it or the manager cancels or reverses it.

Tenants must submit late-payment requests before the due date starts in Dubai. Rent must be paid before the due date starts. Managers can record late external payments. The due date counts as the first late day.

Allow advance rent when the tenant names the future month. Apply a payment to the named month first. For any amount without a month designation, apply it to the oldest outstanding rent first and then to the next outstanding rent. Mark any excess as a refund due. Show the refund amount and status to both parties. The manager returns the excess and records the refund.
Use cash basis only for financial reports. Count income when received and expenses when paid, regardless of payment method. Keep unpaid obligations and arrears visible as operational records.
Split shared costs equally across occupied rental spaces. Apply a new split from the start of the next calendar month.
Require the manager declaration, proof of ownership or tenancy, and written landlord consent where applicable before unit activation.
Warn users about expired required identity, licence, or property documents. Block new contracts that rely on an expired document. Existing contracts and normal account access remain available.

Let rejected applicants resubmit after correction. Let suspended tenants read their own contract and payment history. Use support for closed-relationship reports and documents if the account is suspended, per DEC-26.
Accept PDF, JPG, and PNG up to 10 MB. Verification codes expire after 10 minutes and allow five attempts. Invitations expire after seven days. Send one reminder two days before expiry.
Support 500 units, 100 concurrent users, and 10,000 rows per report. Target the 95th percentile at or below two seconds for normal pages and 60 seconds for reports.
After a no-change review, wait until the next same-space anniversary. After a deferral, send one reminder on the new date.
Require authenticator-app MFA before privileged administrator access. Allow read-only support impersonation with a required reason and audit entry.
Require tenant confirmation in the app before an initial contract or a later rent change takes effect.
Give former tenants read-only access to their own past reports and documents. For a suspended account, route requests for closed-relationship reports and documents through support.
